title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment, Reference Architectures, Day-2 Ops, and Upgrade/Rollback Guide
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Summary
------
This document consolidates our recommended deployment patterns for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem), provides canonical reference architectures, details packaging and installation options, and defines operational day-2 procedures including monitoring, backups, capacity management, and explicit upgrade + rollback playbooks. Intended as the single source of truth for SREs, solutions engineers, and customers running production Redwood Private clusters.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: VPC-hosted private control plane, customer-managed VPCs, and fully on-prem air-gapped installations. Includes reference hardware/node profiles, network/firewall requirements, install options (Helm and on-prem installer), day-2 runbooks, and upgrade/rollback procedures.
- Audience: Platform / SRE teams, Solutions Engineers (pre-sales/onboarding), Customer infra teams, and Support escalation engineers.

Prerequisites
-------------
- Supported Kubernetes: upstream 1.25-1.28 (CNI-compatible).
- Minimum connectivity for VPC mode: outbound HTTPS (443) to control-plane.redwood.ai endpoints for telemetry and license checks (if customer opts in).
- On-prem air-gapped: container registry mirror + TAR bundles of Helm charts and images.
- RBAC: cluster-admin during install; post-install operators run under dedicated namespace and service accounts.

Reference architectures
-----------------------
1) VPC (recommended for most enterprise customers)
   - Components: customer-apps -> customer ingress (ALB/NLB) -> cluster -> Redwood Private control plane (in customer-managed VPC) -> optional NAT/Gateway to Redwood updates
   - High-level diagram (text):
     - Public Internet
       -> Customer VPN/Direct Connect -> Customer VPC (Private Subnets)
       -> EKS/GKE/AKS worker nodes + control plane namespace "redwood"
       -> Internal services: runtime-proxy, kv-cache, autoscaler, model-store gateway
   - Sizing guidance:
     Table: component | min CPUs | min RAM | replication
     - control-plane | 4 | 16GB | 3 replicas (HA)
     - runtime-proxy | 8 | 32GB | 2+ GPUs or 4+ CPU replicas for CPU mode
     - model-store | 4 | 16GB | 2 replicas
   - Network requirements (short): allow egress 443 to updates; allow internal ports 50051 (gRPC), 8080 (HTTP) between services.

2) On-prem (air-gapped / regulated)
   - Components packaged as OCI images and Helm charts mirrored to customer registry.
   - Recommended topology: VLANs for management, inference, and storage. Separate GPU cluster for inference nodes; separate management cluster for control plane when air gap required.
   - Storage: NFS or S3-compatible object store for model artifacts (min throughput 500 MB/s aggregate for large model pulls).
   - Hardware guidance (example): GPU nodes (NVIDIA A100/RTX6000 equivalent), 8+ cores, 256GB RAM, NVMe local for /var/lib/docker; control plane nodes: 16 cores, 64GB, 2TB SSD.

Packaging & installation options
-------------------------------
- Helm (preferred for managed Kubernetes):
  1. Add chart repo: helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai/stable
  2. Preflight: helm upgrade --install redwood-preflight redwood/preflight -f customer/preflight-values.yaml
  3. Install: helm upgrade --install redwood redwood/private --namespace redwood -f customer/values.yaml
- On-prem installer (air-gapped): provide TAR bundle + install script: ./install.sh --mirror /path/to/registry-mirror.tar.gz --values ./values-onprem.yaml
- Post-install checks (automated):
  - kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood --watch (all pods Running and Ready within 10m)
  - /opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl status (returns green)

Network & security checklist (example)
-------------------------------------
- Firewall rules: allow intra-cluster ports 50051/tcp, 8080/tcp, 9090/tcp; allow outbound 443 to updates endpoint if not air-gapped.
- TLS: mTLS enabled by default between components; customer should provide CA or use built-in self-signed certs for PoC.
- Secrets: integrate with KMS/HSM when available; otherwise use sealed-secrets for encrypted manifests.

Day-2 operations (runbook highlights)
------------------------------------
1) Monitoring & observability
   - Required metrics: request_latency_p50/p95/p99, token_throughput, evicted_cache_keys, gpu_utilization, model_load_time.
   - Dashboards: per-route latency, per-model QPS, tail-latency heatmap (90/95/99).
   - Alerting thresholds (examples):
     - P95 latency > 500ms for 5m -> Sev2
     - Error rate > 1% for 10m -> Sev2
     - GPU memory utilisation > 95% sustained 3m -> Capacity alert
2) Backups & disaster recovery
   - Control plane backup cadence: daily etcd snapshot + weekly full config export to external S3. Restore tested quarterly.
   - Model artifacts: keep immutable model versions in object store; replicate to secondary region for critical customers.
3) Capacity planning
   - Autoscaling policies: recommend target CPU 60% / GPU util 70% with burst headroom 30%.
   - Load testing: run synthetic traffic that matches 95th percentile of production prompt length and concurrency before each major rollout.

Upgrade and rollback procedures
-------------------------------
Purpose: ensure safe, reversible updates to control plane and runtime components with minimal user impact.

Pre-upgrade checklist (mandatory)
1. Confirm backups: etcd snapshot and config export completed and verified.
2. Health: all pods Ready, no active Sev1/Sev2 incidents.
3. Canary environment: have separate namespace/cluster or subset of nodes for canary.
4. Migration plan: model format/serialization changes documented.

Upgrade steps (control plane)
1. Bump chart image tag in values.yaml to target release.
2. Apply to canary namespace: helm upgrade --install redwood-canary redwood/private -n redwood-canary -f values-canary.yaml
3. Validate canary for 1-4 hours:
   - smoke tests (auth, route creation, simple inference)
   - regression evals on representative prompt set (fail on >2% quality drop)
4. If canary passes, perform rolling upgrade in production: helm upgrade --install redwood redwood/private -n redwood -f values-prod.yaml --wait --timeout 20m
5. Post-upgrade validation: run end-to-end latency and quality checks; monitor error rates for 30m.

Rollback steps (if upgrade causes regressions)
1. Immediately scale down traffic to the affected model/route (routing policy) if possible.
2. Roll back Helm release: helm rollback redwood <previous_revision> -n redwood
3. If rollback fails, restore control plane from etcd snapshot and config export (documented restore steps).
4. Open incident bridge and notify stakeholders.

Notes on runtime upgrades (GPU nodes)
- GPU node image changes should be staged separately from control plane changes.
- Do not evict all replicas for a hot model at once; use pod disruption budgets to maintain at least 1 replica serving if possible.

Customer requirements library (quick-reference)
--------------------------------------------
- Networking:
  - Private VPC: NAT or egress gateway to allow updates if customer opts in.
  - CIDR recommendations: avoid overlapping with partner networks; use /16 or /20 depending on cluster size.
- Compliance & data residency:
  - For regulated customers, provide option to disable outbound telemetry and route audit logs to customer SIEM.
- Storage:
  - Object store endpoints, credential rotation policy, signed URL TTL recommendations (default 15m).
- Authentication & RBAC:
  - Support for OIDC, SAML through customer IdP; minimum session TTL 1h.

Ownership & escalation
---------------------
- Owning team: eng-private-deployments (primary), eng-sre (shared for runbooks/alerts).
- Oncall escalation path: 1) Oncall SRE -> 2) Private Deployments Pager -> 3) Engineering Manager -> 4) Solutions Eng. Pager details maintained in team wiki.

Appendices
---------
A) Example values.yaml snippet:
```yaml
replicaCount: 3
runtimeProxy:
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: "8"
      memory: "32Gi"
    requests:
      cpu: "4"
      memory: "16Gi"
networking:
  internalGrpcPort: 50051
```
B) Example smoke test commands:
- curl -k https://private-redwood.example.local/healthz
- redwoodctl eval --prompt "Summarize: Redwood Inference" --model rwd-small v2
C) SLOs and targets (exposed to customers):
- API availability: 99.95% monthly (Dedicated SLA)
- P95 inference latency: <= 300ms for small models; <= 800ms for L/R large models depending on sequence length and hardware
